<reason>A high-quality, genuinely contested debate. A built a sophisticated CON case: opt-in gates are porous where protection is needed (cheap signatures under pressure) and rigid where it isn't (holdouts, estates, non-response as the normal case for catalogue work), with a non-waivable collective floor as the superior instrument. B's opening and rebuttals were equally sharp, and B won the decisive framing battle: (1) the bounded-consent answer ("a hiring-day box authorizing everything forever is boilerplate wearing a checkbox costume") neutralized A's claim that opt-in permits the irreversible reuse harm; (2) the necessary-vs-sufficient reframe absorbed A's floor argument — A never showed consent is harmful or redundant alongside floors, only that it needs a partner; (3) B's "boilerplate was never defended" point had real teeth, since A's own world (original license covers dubbing plus bargained limits) still authorizes synthesis via contract signed before the technology existed, leaving the motion's core complaint — the performer is never asked — standing. A's non-response argument was its strongest live route and B answered it only partially and late (registries/proxies first appearing in the closing, a small lateness cost). A also took an execution hit from the clipped Rebuttal 2. Both sides answered pressure questions with proper A1/A2 structure, but B's answers converted A's traps into its own frame more cleanly, and B's closing crystallized the choice (floor caps harm; only consent prevents the silent taking) better than A's recap of the ceremony argument.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2: answering A's two pressure traps directly — distinguishing specific bounded consent from an everything-forever checkbox ("boilerplate wearing a checkbox costume"), then accepting retention caps while reframing the motion as "consent is required, not sufficient" — turned A's strongest attack (the floor does all the real work) into a concession of B's central claim, and set up the undefeated "floor alone still permits the silent taking" closer.</best_rebuttal>
